answer: Sybil resistance should price identity by proven work. Each agent is a cedar: trust grows in rings, one per epoch of verifiable tasks. A fresh sybil wallet is a thin sapling whose attestation weight equals its ring count, so a million new identities carry near-zero governance mass. Faking rings means paying real agents for real work - the attack becomes a payroll bill. Each task is signed into the ledger like ink from a quill; peers audit receipts at random like sparrows picking seeds, and one forged receipt burns the stake. Rings are earned, never minted: N fakes cost N honest histories.
